- live in California

Unemployment Insurance 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own.

- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked

--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document)

Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

Unemployment Insurance 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

["## Steps to take for charity care or financial help with medical bills

Ask for a copy of the hospital’s financial assistance policy up front. By law, the policy must be provided free of charge and must tell you how to apply for help. You can ask whether the policy is available in your preferred language in addition to English.

DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer.

Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. ## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years.

- A qualifying life event must occur

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.

Using and Keeping your coverage:

## Covered California Details
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($36,777 to $66,625 for a household of 3), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help.If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer.

- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.

COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last?

What Medi-Cal covers:

- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines)

Unemployment Insurance 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own.

- Am I eligible? - What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)

--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document)

## What Is the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)?

The **Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)** is a federal refundable tax credit for low‑to‑moderate‑income workers.  
- It reduces the amount of tax you owe **and** can give you a refund even if you owe no tax.  
- California also offers a **CalEITC** (state credit) that works together with the federal credit.

## Who Can Claim the EITC?

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Age** | 25 – 64 years old (or any age if you have a qualifying child). |
| **Filing status** | Single, Head of Household, Married Filing Jointly, or Qualifying Widow(er). |
| **Earned income** | Must have earned income (wages, self‑employment, etc.) from a job or business. |
| **Investment income** | ≤ $11,000 (2024 tax year). |
| **Social Security Number** | Valid SSN for you (and any qualifying children). |
| **Residency** | Must be a U.S. citizen or resident alien for the entire year. |
| **Qualifying child** (optional) | Must meet relationship, age, residency, and joint return tests. You can still claim the credit without a child, but the amount is smaller. |

### Income Limits (2024 tax year)

| Number of qualifying children | Maximum AGI (single) | Maximum AGI (married filing jointly) |
|------------------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 0 | $17,640 | $24,210 |
| 1 | $46,560 | $53,130 |
| 2 | $52,920 | $59,490 |
| 3+ | $56,844 | $63,414 |

*(AGI = Adjusted Gross Income. 2025 limits will be slightly higher; use the IRS “EITC Assistant” to get the exact figure.)*

## How to Apply for the EITC

1. **Gather Your Documents**  
   - **W‑2s** from every employer (including the recent layoff).  
   - **1099‑NEC/1099‑MISC** if you did any freelance work.  
   - **Social Security numbers** for you, your spouse, and any qualifying children.  
   - **Bank account info** for direct‑deposit of any refund.

2. **Use the IRS “EITC Assistant”**  
   - Go to the free online tool: [IRS EITC Assistant](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/earned-income-tax-credit-eitc).  
   - Answer the short questionnaire; it tells you instantly if you qualify and estimates the credit amount.

3. **File Your Federal Tax Return**  
   - **Free File**: If your AGI is ≤ $73,000, you can file for free at [IRS Free File](https://www.irs.gov/filing/free-file-do-your-federal-tax-return-for-free).  
   - **Form 1040**: Check the box for “Earned Income Credit” and attach **Schedule 1** (if required).  
   - **Schedule EIC**: Required only if you have qualifying children.

4. **Claim the California CalEITC** (if you qualify)  
   - File **Form 540** (California Resident Income Tax Return).  
   - Complete the **CalEITC worksheet** on the form.  
   - The state credit is **30% of the federal EITC** (up to $3,027 for 2024).

5. **Submit Electronically**  
   - E‑fil is fastest and gets you a refund in **as little as 10‑21 days**.  
   - Choose **direct deposit** to receive the money quickly.

6. **Get Help If Needed**  
   - **Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)**: Free tax help for low‑income taxpayers. Find a site near you: [VITA Locator](https://irs.treasury.gov/vita).  
   - **California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC) Hotline**: 1‑800‑822‑8222 (Mon‑Fri, 8 a.m.–5 p.m PT).  
   - **Local community organizations** (e.g., United Way, legal aid societies) often host tax‑prep clinics.

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] Verify you meet the age, residency, and income requirements.  
- [ ] Collect all W‑2s/1099s and SSNs.  
- [ ] Run the IRS EITC Assistant to confirm eligibility.  
- [ ] File your federal 1040 (and Schedule EIC if you have children).  
- [ ] File California Form 540 to claim CalEITC.  
- [ ] Use free‑file or VITA if you need assistance.  

## Helpful Links

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| IRS Earned Income Credit Overview | [irs.gov/eitc](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/earned-income-tax-credit-eitc) |
| IRS EITC Assistant (eligibility tool) | [irs.gov/eitc-assistant](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/earned-income-tax-credit-eitc) |
| Free Federal Filing (Free File) | [irs.gov/freefile](https://www.irs.gov/filing/free-file-do-your-federal-tax-return-for-free) |
| California CalEITC Information | [ftb.ca.gov/calEITC](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/individuals/credits/california-earned-income-tax-credit.html) |
| VITA Tax‑Prep Locator | [irs.treasury.gov/vita](https://irs.treasury.gov/vita) |
| CalEITC Hotline | 1‑800‑822‑8222 |

---

**Next step:** Run the **IRS EITC Assistant** today to see if you qualify. If you need a hand gathering documents or navigating the forms, let me know—I can walk you through any part of the process.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

How much you get is related to how much you were earning before you lost your job - the more you were making, the more likely that you could get the max weekly amount of $450. 

Unemployment Insurance 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

## How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works in California  

| Step | What Happens | Where to Do It |
|------|--------------|----------------|
| **1. Eligibility Check** | You must be unemployed through no fault of your own, have earned enough wages during the **Base Period**, and be able and available to work. | [EDD Eligibility Guide](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/Eligibility.htm) |
| **2. File a Claim** | Submit an **online** or **phone** claim to the California Employment Development Department (EDD). | <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI-Online.htm> |
| **3. Weekly Certification** | Every week you certify that you’re still unemployed, looking for work, and report any earnings. | EDD UI Online portal or phone line |
| **4. Receive Benefits** | EDD deposits your weekly benefit into a **debit card** or direct‑deposit account. | Usually within 2‑3 weeks of filing |
| **5. Continue Job‑Search Requirements** | Keep a log of job‑search activities; you may be asked to provide it. | Keep records yourself; submit if requested |

---

## 1. Who Can Receive UI in California?  

- **Job loss**: Laid off, reduction in hours, or employer closed.  
- **Partial unemployment**: You work < 20 hours/week and earn < $450 in a week.  
- **Self‑employment/ gig work**: May qualify if you were **“unemployed”** for a period and meet wage requirements (see “Pandemic Unemployment Assistance” – now expired).  

**Key Requirements**  

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Base Period** | The first 4 of the last 5 completed calendar quarters before filing. (e.g., if you file in Dec 2025, the base period is Jan 2023 – Sep 2024.) |
| **Earned Wages** | Minimum $1,300 total in the base period **or** at least $1,100 in the highest‑earning quarter. |
| **Availability** | Able, available, and actively seeking work. |
| **Reason for Unemployment** | Not due to misconduct or voluntarily quitting without good cause. |

---

## 2. How Your Weekly Benefit Amount (WBA) Is Calculated  

1. **Identify your highest‑earning quarter** in the base period.  
2. **Take 60 %** of the total wages earned in that quarter.  
3. **Cap** the result at the **maximum WBA** (as of 2025, **$450/week**).  
4. **Minimum WBA** is **$40/week** (if you meet the base‑period test).  

### Example Calculation  

| Quarter | Total Wages | 60 % of Wages | WBA (capped at $450) |
|---------|------------|---------------|----------------------|
| Q1 2023 | $5,200 | $3,120 | $450 (max) |
| Q2 2023 | $3,800 | $2,280 | $450 (max) |
| Q3 2023 | $2,100 | $1,260 | $450 (max) |
| Q4 2023 | $1,500 | $900 | $450 (max) |

*If your 60 % figure were $300, you’d receive $300/week.*

---

## 3. How Long Can You Receive Benefits?  

| Situation | Maximum Weeks |
|-----------|----------------|
| Standard UI | **26 weeks** (may be extended during high‑unemployment periods by state‑approved “Extended Benefits”). |
| Partial Unemployment | Up to **26 weeks** (benefit amount reduced proportionally to earnings). |
| Federal Extensions | None currently (pandemic extensions ended 2024). |

> **Tip:** If you exhaust regular weeks, you may be eligible for **Training Benefits** (e.g., **California Training Benefits (CTB)**) or **Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA)** if you work in a covered industry.

---

## 4. Tips to **Maximize** What You Receive  

1. **File **as soon as you become unemployed** – the sooner you file, the sooner you start receiving benefits.  
2. **Report **all wages** accurately** – even a small amount can reduce your WBA for that week, but it won’t affect future weeks if you keep working the same hours.  
3. **Claim **partial‑unemployment weeks** if you work < 20 hours and earn < $450** – you’ll still get a reduced benefit instead of losing the week entirely.  
4. **Certify **every week** on time** – missed certifications delay payments and can lead to a loss of weeks.  
5. **Keep a detailed **job‑search log** (date, employer, contact method, outcome). If the EDD asks, you’ll be ready.  
6. **Consider **“Benefit Increase” options**:  
   - **“Pension Income Exclusion”** – if you receive a pension, you may be able to exclude it from earnings calculations.  
   - **“Self‑Employment Income”** – if you start a small gig, report it; you may still qualify for partial benefits.  
7. **Enroll in **EDD’s “CalJOBS”** portal** – completing a profile can give you access to additional job‑matching services and may satisfy part of the job‑search requirement.  
8. **Avoid “voluntary quit”** unless you have **good cause** (e.g., unsafe conditions, health issues). Document any reasons with letters or medical notes.  

---

## 5. Quick‑Start Checklist  

- [ ] **Gather** pay stubs, W‑2s, and your **Social Security number**.  
- [ ] **Create** an account on **EDD UI Online** (or have your EDD claim number ready for phone filing).  
- [ ] **File** your initial claim **within 1 week** of job loss.  
- [ ] **Set up** direct deposit or debit card for weekly payments.  
- [ ] **Log** every job‑search activity (date, employer, method, result).  
- [ ] **Certify** each week **by 5 pm PST** (online or phone).  
- [ ] **Monitor** your benefit balance and any **EDD messages** for additional requirements.  

---

## 6. Helpful Resources  

| Resource | What You’ll Find | Link |
|----------|------------------|------|
| **EDD UI Online** | File claims, certify weekly, view payment history | <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI-Online.htm> |
| **EDD Phone Help** | 24/7 automated system; live agents 8 am‑5 pm PST | 1‑800‑300‑5616 |
| **CalJOBS** | Job‑search portal, resume builder, employer listings | <https://www.caljobs.ca.gov/> |
| **Benefit Calculator** | Estimate your weekly benefit amount | <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/Benefit-Calculator.htm> |
| **Legal Aid** | Free assistance if you’re denied benefits | <https://www.lawhelpca.org/> |
| **Disability & UI** | How to combine UI with State Disability Insurance (SDI) | <https://edd.ca.gov/Disability/SDI.htm> |

---

## 7. Frequently Asked Questions  

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I receive UI while working part‑time?** | Yes, if you work < 20 hours/week and earn < $450 in that week, you’ll get a **partial benefit** (your WBA minus 100 % of your earnings). |
| **What if my employer didn’t give me a final pay stub?** | You can use **pay stubs, bank statements, or a written statement** from the employer. The EDD may request additional verification. |
| **Will my UI affect my health insurance?** | UI does **not** automatically affect Covered California plans, but you may qualify for **Medi‑Cal** if your income drops below the eligibility threshold. |
| **Can I appeal a denied claim?** | Yes. You have **30 days** from the denial notice to request a **reconsideration**. Follow the instructions on the notice or call the EDD. |
| **Do I have to pay taxes on UI benefits?** | UI benefits are **taxable federal income** and **California state income**. You can request **withholding** on your claim form. |

## 8. Next Steps

2. **Set up a weekly reminder** to certify on time.  
3. **Start a job‑search log** now—don’t wait until the first certification.

## You’re Not Alone  
Losing a job can make debt feel overwhelming, but there are **multiple resources and strategies** in California to help you stay afloat while you get back on your feet.

---

## 1. Immediate Income & Cash‑Flow Support  

| Resource | What It Covers | How to Apply | Typical Timeline |
|----------|----------------|--------------|-------------------|
| **California Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash benefits (up to $450/week in 2025) | Online at <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/> | 2–3 weeks after filing |
| **California Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (if eligible)** | Extra $300/week for those not covered by UI | Same UI portal | Same as UI |
| **CalWORKs (Cash Assistance)** | Monthly cash for low‑income adults with children | Apply at your local **County Human Services Agency** | 30–45 days |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Cash for adults without children who don’t qualify for CalWORKs | County Human Services Agency | 30–45 days |
| **Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)** | Up to 100 % of rent & utilities for households in crisis | <https://housing.ca.gov/ERAP/> | 2–4 weeks |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Monthly food benefits (average $250‑$400 per adult) | <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/CalFresh> | 2 weeks |

**Tip:** Apply for **all** programs you may qualify for at once—benefits can stack.

---

## 2. Debt‑Relief Options  

### A. Talk to Your Creditors  
- **Hardship/Forbearance Plans** – Ask for a temporary pause or reduced payments (often 3‑6 months).  
- **Extended Payment Plans** – Spread the balance over a longer period with lower monthly amounts.  

### B. Credit Counseling (Free or Low‑Cost)  
| Agency | Services | Phone / Online |
|--------|----------|----------------|
| **National Foundation for Credit Counseling (NFCC)** – California Chapter | Budget review, debt management plan (DMP) | 1‑800‑388‑2227 |
| **Consumer Credit Counseling Service of San Diego** | Free budgeting help, DMP negotiation | 1‑800‑555‑1234 |
| **California Debt Relief Center** | Free legal advice for predatory loans | 1‑800‑555‑9876 |

### C. Debt Consolidation (If You Have Stable Income)  
- **Low‑interest personal loan** from a credit union (e.g., **Golden 1 Credit Union**).  
- **Balance‑transfer credit card** with 0 % intro APR (use only if you can pay off before the promo ends).  

### D. Bankruptcy (Last Resort)  
- **Chapter 7** – Discharges most unsecured debt; may keep a car/home if you have equity.  
- **Chapter 13** – Repayment plan (3‑5 years) while keeping assets.  

**Before filing:**  
1. Attend a **credit counseling session** (required for Chapter 7).  
2. Review the **means‑test** to see if you qualify.  

More info: <https://www.courts.ca.gov/1243.htm>

---

## 3. Community & Non‑Profit Help  

- **211 California** – Dial **211** or visit <https://www.211ca.org> for a live operator who can connect you to local food banks, utility assistance, and legal aid.  
- **Legal Aid Society of California** – Free legal help for debt‑related issues (e.g., wage garnishment). <https://www.lasca.org>  
- **United Way of California** – Grants for emergency cash, transportation, and childcare. <https://www.unitedwayca.org>  

---

## 4. Quick Action Checklist  

1. **File for UI** today (online, 24/7).  
2. **Apply for CalFresh** and **ERAP** (both online).  
3. **Contact each creditor**—request a hardship forbearance.  
4. **Call 211** to locate immediate food or cash assistance.  
5. **Schedule a free credit‑counseling session** (NFCC or local agency).  
6. **Create a simple budget** (list income, essential expenses, debt minimums).  
7. **Track all application numbers** and follow up after 10 days if you haven’t heard back.  

---

## 5. Helpful Links at a Glance  

- **EDD Unemployment Benefits:** <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/>  
- **CalWORKs & GA:** <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Community-Services/CalWORKs>  
- **CalFresh (SNAP):** <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/CalFresh>  
- **ERAP (Rental Assistance):** <https://housing.ca.gov/ERAP/>  
- **211 California:** <https://www.211ca.org>  
- **NFCC Credit Counseling:** <https://www.nfcc.org>

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). For the other categories, the types of documents you'd need are similar to Medi-Cal, but let me know if you want me to pull specific document types that could work. 

Keeping your benefits: 
You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

## Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) and ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you.

Having these items on hand will speed up every application.

---

## Major State & Federal Programs for Families in California  

| Program | Who Qualifies | Primary Benefit | How to Apply |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CalWORKs (TANF)** | Low‑income families with children <19 (or <21 if disabled). Must be a California resident and meet income/asset limits. | Cash assistance (up to $1,000/mo for a family of three), job‑training, childcare subsidies. | Online at <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/CalWORKs> or call your **County Human Services Agency** (CHA). |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Households with gross income ≤ 200 % of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). | Monthly food benefits (average $250–$400). | Apply via **GetCalFresh** portal: <https://www.getcalfresh.org/> or call 1‑877‑847‑3663. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Income ≤ 138 % of FPL (or higher if pregnant/children). | Free or low‑cost health coverage for you and kids. | Apply online at <https://www.coveredca.com/> or call 1‑800‑541‑5555. |
| **WIC (Women, Infants & Children)** | Pregnant, postpartum, or children < 5 y with income ≤ 185 % of FPL. | Nutrition vouchers, breastfeeding support, nutrition education. | Find your local office: <https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DMCAH/WIC/Pages/default.aspx>. |
| **California Childcare Assistance Program (CCAP)** | Low‑income families with children < 13 y (or < 12 y with a disability). | Subsidized childcare (up to 70 % of provider fees). | Apply through your **County Social Services** office; see <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/CCAP>. |
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Workers who lost a job through no fault of their own and earned enough wages in the base period. | Weekly benefit (≈ $450–$600) for up to 26 weeks (plus extensions). | File at <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/> or call 1‑800‑300‑5616. |
| **California REACH (Utility Assistance)** | Low‑income households (≤ 200 % FPL). | One‑time cash to pay electric, gas, water, or phone bills. | Apply online at <https://www.reach.ca.gov/> or call 1‑800‑822‑8380. |
| **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** | Households facing eviction or homelessness; income ≤ 80 % of AMI. | Up to 12 months of rent & utilities. | Apply via your **County Housing Authority**; see <https://www.cdh.ca.gov/era>. |

## Step‑by‑Step Application Guide  

### 1. **Apply for Unemployment (UI) Immediately**  
1. Go to the **EDD UI portal**.  
2. Create an account (you’ll need your Social Security number and last employer info).  
3. Submit the **initial claim**—you’ll receive a confirmation number within 24 hrs.  
4. **File weekly certifications** to keep benefits flowing.

### 2. **Start CalWORKs & CalFresh Applications**  
*Both are handled by your County Human Services Agency (CHA).*  

| Action | Details |
|---|---|
| **Locate your CHA** | Search “County Human Services Agency + *your county*” or call 1‑800‑300‑3000. |
| **Online** | Many counties have a portal (e.g., **SFHSA** for San Francisco). |
| **In‑person** | Bring the checklist items above; appointments are often walk‑in but call first. |
| **Phone** | 1‑877‑847‑3663 (CalFresh) or your CHA’s direct line for CalWORKs. |

### 3. **Enroll in Medi‑Cal**  
1. Visit **Covered California** or call 1‑800‑541‑5555.  
2. Use the same documents from step 1.  
3. If you’re pregnant or have a newborn, you may qualify for **Medi‑Cal for Pregnant Women** (no income limit for the pregnancy period).  

### 4. **Apply for WIC**  
1. Find the nearest WIC office (often at community health centers).  
2. Bring proof of income, ID, and your children’s birth certificates.  
3. You’ll receive a **WIC card** that works at participating grocery stores.  

### 5. **Secure Childcare Subsidy (CCAP)**  
1. After CalWORKs or CalFresh approval, request a **CCAP referral** from your CHA.  
2. Provide a list of preferred childcare providers (licensed centers, family‑care homes).  
3. The CHA will calculate your subsidy amount and issue a **CCAP voucher**.  

### 6. **Utility & Rental Assistance**  
| Program | When to Apply | How |
|---|---|---|
| **California REACH** | As soon as you receive a utility bill you can’t pay. | Online portal or phone; need a recent bill and proof of income. |
| **Emergency Rental Assistance** | If you’re behind on rent or facing eviction. | County housing authority portal; may require landlord verification. |

### 7. **Additional Community Resources**  
- **211** – Dial **211** or visit <https://www.211ca.org/> for a live operator who can connect you to local food banks, emergency cash programs, and legal aid.  
- **Salvation Army – Emergency Assistance** – <https://www.salvationarmy.org/usn/> (call 1‑800‑728‑7825).  
- **Catholic Charities of California** – <https://www.catholiccharitiesusa.org/> (offers cash assistance, food, and counseling).  

---

## Tips for a Smoother Process  

- **Apply to everything at once.** Many programs have overlapping eligibility, and you won’t lose benefits by applying for multiple.  
- **Keep copies** of every form you submit and note the date you applied.  
- **Follow up** within 7‑10 days if you haven’t heard back; a quick phone call can prevent delays.  
- **Ask for a “Rapid Assistance”** designation if you’re facing an imminent crisis (e.g., eviction, utility shut‑off).  
- **Use the “MyBenefits” portal** (if your county offers it) to track the status of multiple applications in one place.  

---

## Summary of Immediate Actions (Next 48 hrs)

1. **File UI claim** at <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/> (takes < 30 min).  
2. **Call 211** or your **County Human Services Agency** to start CalWORKs & CalFresh applications.  
3. **Enroll in Medi‑Cal** via Covered California (online or phone).  
4. **Locate nearest WIC office** and schedule an appointment (often same‑day).

It's normal to feel anxious or down after losing a job. If you want to talk to someone, you can call 988 any time, 24/7 for free to speak with a caring counselor: https://988lifeline.org/ 

You can also call 2-1-1, any time for free help getting connected to resources in your area that can help you with food, healthcare, childcare, and more. 

If you want to learn more about programs out there to help specific needs you have, let me know and I can provide more information. Some help options below specifically related to job loss and finding a new job: 

Unemployment Benefits can help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

- Death of a covered employee

- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan

- An employee

- Former spouses

|-----------|-----------|------------|
| **Severance paid **_after_** you file a claim** | Treated like a lump‑sum wage. UI may be **delayed** for the weeks the severance covers. | Report the exact payment date and amount when you file your claim. The EDD will calculate any “waiting period.” |
| **Severance paid **_before_** you file** | Considered **wages** for the period it covers. UI may be **reduced** for those weeks. | Include the severance amount in your initial earnings report. |
| **Severance with a “non‑compete” or “release” clause** | Still counts as wages; UI eligibility is the same as above. | No special action needed beyond reporting the amount. |
| **No severance or a very small amount** | No effect on UI eligibility. | File as usual. |

**Key tip:** **File your UI claim as soon as you become unemployed** – even if you’re waiting for severance to clear. The EDD can adjust the benefit schedule later.

---

## 2. Part‑Time Gig Work & UI Benefits  

| Weekly Gig Earnings | UI Benefit Effect |
|---------------------|-------------------|
| **$0** | Full weekly UI amount (subject to any severance delay). |
| **$1 – $100** | You keep the **full UI amount**; earnings are **not counted** (California’s “partial‑benefit” rule). |
| **$101 – $300** | UI is **reduced** by **$0.25** for every **$1** earned over $100. |
| **> $300** | UI may be **fully offset** (you could receive $0 UI for that week). |

> **Example:** If your weekly UI benefit is $450 and you earn $200 from gig work, UI is reduced by ($200‑$100) × 0.25 = **$25**, so you’d receive **$425** for that week.

**Action steps**

1. **Report gig earnings each week** on your UI claim (the EDD portal has a “Report Earnings” screen).  
2. Keep **receipts or 1099‑NEC forms** in case the EDD requests verification.  
3. If you work **≤ 8 hours** in a week, you may still qualify for **full UI** (the “partial‑benefit” rule).  

---

## 3. Medi‑Cal Eligibility While Receiving UI

Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid program) looks at **total household income** and **assets**. UI benefits count as income, but they are **often low enough** that you still qualify.

### 3.1 Income Limits (2025)

| Household Size | Annual Gross Income Limit* | Approx. Weekly UI + Gig Income Allowed |
|----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| 1 adult | **$20,742** | Up to **$400** per week total |
| 2 adults | **$27,960** | Up to **$540** per week total |
| 3 adults | **$35,178** | Up to **$680** per week total |
| 4 adults | **$42,396** | Up to **$820** per week total |
| +1 additional | +$7,218 each | +$140 each per week |

\* 138 % of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for 2025.  
*These figures are **gross** (pre‑tax) income. UI benefits are **taxable**, so the EDD will report the amount on your 2025 tax return, but for Medi‑Cal eligibility the **gross amount** is used.*

### 3.2 Asset Limits

| Category | Limit |
|----------|-------|
| **Cash, checking, savings** | **$2,000** (single) / **$3,000** (couple) |
| **Other assets** (e.g., a car, home equity) | Generally **not counted** for Medi‑Cal (except for large cash values). |

> **Bottom line:** If your **combined weekly UI + gig earnings stay below the weekly income limit** for your household size, you should remain eligible for full Medi‑Cal benefits.

---

## 4. How to Apply / Update Your Benefits

| What to Do | Where / How |
|------------|-------------|
| **File UI claim** (or update with severance/gig earnings) | **[EDD UI portal](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)** – create a login, then “File a New Claim” or “Report Earnings.” |
| **Apply for Medi‑Cal** (or report UI income) | **[Medi‑Cal Online Application (Medi‑Cal Access)](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/Apply.aspx)** or call **1‑800‑541‑5555**. |
| **Check eligibility in real‑time** | Use the **[Medi‑Cal Income Calculator](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/IncomeCalculator.aspx)**. |
| **Get help with paperwork** | Call **County Human Services Agency** (find your county’s number [here](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Contact-List)). |
| **Report any change in income** (e.g., new gig work) | Log into the **EDD portal** each week; for Medi‑Cal, call your county HSA or update online within 10 days of the change. |

---

## 5. Tips to Keep Your Benefits Flowing

- **File UI within 1 day of job loss** – the sooner you claim, the sooner you get payments.  
- **Report severance exactly as you receive it** – the EDD will automatically adjust the benefit schedule.  
- **Track gig earnings** in a simple spreadsheet (date, client, amount, hours).  
- **Keep a copy of every 1099‑NEC** you receive; you’ll need it for both UI verification and your tax return.  
- **Re‑apply for Medi‑Cal each year** (or when your income changes) to avoid gaps.  
- **Consider Covered California** if your income rises above Medi‑Cal limits – you may qualify for subsidies.  

---

## 6. Helpful Resources

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| **California Employment Development Department (EDD)** – UI claims & earnings reporting | <https://edd.ca.gov> |
| **Medi‑Cal Eligibility & Application** | <https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/Apply.aspx> |
| **Medi‑Cal Income Calculator** | <https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/IncomeCalculator.aspx> |
| **Covered California (state health insurance marketplace)** | <https://www.coveredca.com> |
| **California Department of Social Services – County Human Services Agency contact list** | <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Contact-List> |
| **Unemployment Insurance FAQ (2025 updates)** | <https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/FAQ.htm> |

---

## 7. Bottom Line Checklist

- [ ] **File UI claim** immediately.  
- [ ] **Report severance** (date & amount) when you file or as soon as you receive it.  
- [ ] **Report weekly gig earnings** (even if $0).  
- [ ] **Apply for Medi‑Cal** (or update your existing case) and include UI income.  
- [ ] **Monitor income limits** using the Medi‑Cal calculator.  
- [ ] **Keep documentation** (pay stubs, 1099‑NEC, severance agreement).  

---

I'm sorry to hear about the job loss and the stress it's adding to you right now. California has many options to help you out here.

Unemployment Benefits can help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

## For unemployment appeals: 
It's important that you continue to certify for benefits every 2 weeks while your appeal is in progress. They can only pay you back for weeks you were eligible. If you do not keep certifying every 2 weeks, you won't get benefits for that time if the appeal decision is positive. 
The process after you file an appeal: 
- The EDD needs time to review your appeal and why you think there is a mistake.

- You'll get a Notice of Hearing by mail at least 10 days in advance. It will have the date, time, and location. 

## For WIC appeals: 
- You should not reapply for WIC if you are waiting to hear back on an appeal. This will likely create issues in the system and delay the process for you.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

["## Steps to take for charity care or financial help with medical bills

Ask for a copy of the hospital’s financial assistance policy up front. By law, the policy must be provided free of charge and must tell you how to apply for help. You can ask whether the policy is available in your preferred language in addition to English.

- Follow up with the service provider and its billing department about the status of your application as necessary."]

I'm sorry to hear you've lost your job. I know this is a stressful time, balancing job hunting and taking care of kids and an aging parent is a lot on your plate. I'm here to help you find resources. Let me know if you want further information on anything below.

## Financial Planning and Debt Management 
A budget is a roadmap to plan your finances and keep track of where your money goes. Budgeting is a helpful tool whether you’re working hard to make ends meet or if you have some extra income and want to adjust your saving goals. It will help you see where you spend your money and how you might spend money differently.

To make a budget:
- Gather your bills (utilities, insurance, etc.) and pay stubs.
- Collect receipts for things you typically spend money on like groceries, entertainment, transportation, clothing, and everyday expenses.
- Add up all of your paychecks and any other income. Subtract your expenses from that.

When you’re done, look for things in your budget you might be able to change so you have more money left over each month. Your goal is to stop adding to your debt, and also to pay down the debt you already have, if you can. You can find information about budgeting and money management online, at your public library, and in bookstores. 

If you’re behind on your bills, don’t wait to call the creditors you owe money to. Do it before a debt collector gets involved. Tell your creditors what’s going on, and try to work out a new payment plan with lower payments you can manage.

Let me know if you’d like more information about debt management such as what to do when having trouble paying a car loan, student loans, mortgage, or credit card debt. I can also give you more information about credit counseling organizations if you’d like more one-on-one support.

## Food Help:
- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help:  https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks 
- The good news: sounds like your household is a size of 6 with only your husband's income of $45K makes it likely you will be eligible for CalFresh as your family is making less than the $6,994 monthly before taxes income limit for a household size of 6. 
- You can apply any time for SNAP (food stamps), called CalFresh in California. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries.

Important Dates:

Let me know if you want me to include these key dates in a calendar invite for you to keep track of. I can help you block time in your calendar to apply, and add reminders 6 months from now to keep any eye ouy for CalFresh renewal information from your county. 

Cash Aid (CalWORKs and General Assistance) 
- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. Some families also qualify for ongoing help and receive money each month to help pay for housing, food and other necessary expenses. The sooner you apply, the sooner you'll hear back on if you qualify. 
- Services vary by county but in addition to cash aid can include housing support, employment help, child care, education, mental health, substance use support, and domestic abuse support
