Once you have all your documents, applying should take 30-60 minutes. Would you like me to schedule a calendar block for this time for you to apply? I can also provide a more detailed list of the documents you would need, but generally: ID, proof you live in California, money you recieve, expenses. 
Key Dates: your county will tell you the kinds of change you need to report and by when, but usually within 10 days.  To keep your benefits, your county will also reach out once a year but each program has different requirements. I can also add a reminder to your calendar a year from now? 

Unemployment Benefits can also help ease financial strain while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

California also offers a lot of options finding a new job: 
- Workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching. 

California also has many options to help you with rent, utilities, and more when falling on hard times. 

Rent or mortgage help: 
Calling 2-1-1 in California is the best way to find help to pay your rent, mortgage, utilities bills to stay in your home. Call to speak to someone right away. They will ask you a few questions about your current living situation, any income, any children or dependents who live with you. Even if you don't qualify for a government program, the state or local agency may refer you to a community organization or nonprofit in your area. 

First, you should talk with your landlord if you rent or lender if you have a mortgage to discuss your situation. There may be options like payment plans that could help you stay in your home. Don't stop paying your bills. Seek help early. If you want to talk to someone, the US Department of Housing and Urban Development offers a large network of housing counseling agencies that can help. Search for ones close to you here: https://answers.hud.gov/housingcounseling/s/?language=en_US  

It's important you know your rights. Protections against eviction and foreclosure vary by state. You can search here for more information about eviction and rent protections in California: https://legalfaq.org/covid/ca#state-problems 

Housing Support: 
If you are applying for or already get CalWORKS - California's TANF program - you may also be able to get help through their Housing Support Program or Homeless Assistance program if you are experiencing homelessness now or at risk. This program is run at the county level so contact them if you would like to learn more. If you tell me your county, I can pull addresses and phone numbers for you?
The Housing Support Program can help families find temporary shelter while finding permanent housing, help with moving costs, short to medium term rent support, and a case manager to talk to and work with to get back on your feet. 
The Homeless Assistance program is more focused on helping you cover costs of keeping permanent housing providing payments every 12 months for temporary shelter, and payments to get housing including help with security deposits, last month's rent or up to 2 months of rent.

Find shelters and temporary housing through HUD programs like their local homeless assistance list, their homeless continuing care program provider, and local public housing agencies: https://www.usa.gov/emergency-housing 


There are also programs available to help with internet and phone, lower cost auto insurance, weatherizing your home, and utilities.

Covering phone bills: 
The California Lifeline program gives discounts on home and cell phone services to eligible households. You can get the discount on your home phone or cell phone but not on both. 
Types of Benefits: you can get up to a $19 monthly discount for flat rate service or cell phone service, a service connection discount $39, and certain taxes and user fees are made free 
Eligibility: You can qualify two ways. One way is if you or someone else in your household is already getting help from other programs like Medi-Cal, Low Income Energy Assistance Program, SSI, public hosing, CalFresh, WIC, school lunch, TANF/CalWORKs, and certain veterans program. The second way is based on income. If your household income before taxes is at or below specific limits. Sounds like you have 6 people in your household, and with only your husband making 45K, you are likely eligible for this program (before tax annual income max is $66,600). 
How to apply: First, call your home or cell phone company and tell them you qualify based on the program or income criteria above. They will begin the application for you and in a week you will get an application form in the mail in a pink envelope. You can also apply online by creating an account here: https://www.californialifeline.com/en  You must submit the application and any needed documents by the due date.
Renew Benefits: You will be mailed a renewal form in another pink envelope from the California Lifeline Administrator 105 days prior to your California Lifeline anniversary date. You can renew online or fill out that application and provide any documents they ask for.

Lowering your energy bills and helping pay your energy bills:
High energy bills (Weatherization Assistance Program or WAP): if you notice cold drafts in your home from windows or doors, run the heat all day in winter or the AC all day in the summer, then you may benefit getting a test done on your home called an energy audit. It will be done by a community partner and they may recommend changes like sealing holes and cracks around doors, windows, pipes, checking that your home is insulated, repairing or replacing windows, checking the heating / AC, repairing or replacing water heaters. 
Eligibility and applying: Applying is the best way to know if you can get help from this. For a household of 6, before tax income can't be over about $7,191 a month. Energy use and other factors may affect eligibility for services. This program also often prioritizes applicants based on the greatest need, income, and households with vulnerable populations (elderly, disabled, and households with young children). 
Apply: You need to contact your local provider in your county to apply. You can call them or go on their website for more details on how to apply.
Paying bills (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program or LIHEAP): ​​LIHEAP can offer a one-time payment to help you pay your heating or cooling bills, even if you use wood, propane, or oil. They can also help in an emergency or energy crisis, such as a utility disconnection.​​
LIHEAP can also provide in-home weatherization services for iImproved energy efficiency; and health and safety.​​​​
Eligibility: For a household of 6, you can't make more pre-tax than $8,047 a month. But applying is the best way to know if you can get help. 

Both LIHEAP and WAP are run through your county. Community Service agencies can include everything from food assistance to employment training, education services, housing assistance, emergency services, and more and are also at the county level. Visit the Service Map tool to find one near you to apply: https://www.csd.ca.gov/energybills 

Other programs are available as well in California, if you are not eligible for LIHEAP or WAP, such as:
- California Alternate Rates for Energy (CARE): you can potentially receive a 30-35 percent discount on their electric bill and potentially a 20 percent discount on their natural gas bill. 
- The Family Electric Rate Assistance Program (FERA): Families whose household income slightly exceeds the CARE allowances will qualify to receive FERA discounts, about an 18% discount on their electricity bill. FERA is available for customers of Southern California Edison, San Diego Gas and Electric Company, and Pacific Gas and Electric Company. Call your electric utility to see if your family qualifies.
- The Energy Savings Assistance Program (ESA): gives no-cost weatherization services to low-income households who meet the CARE income guidelines. Services provided include attic insulation, energy efficient refrigerators, energy efficient furnaces, weatherstripping, caulking, low-flow showerheads, water heater blankets, and door and building envelope repairs which reduce air infiltration.

Low cost auto insurance: 
California program that helps good drivers who meet certain income requirements get auto insurance that meets California's state mandatory auto insurance law. You can get up to 2 policies (two vehicles) and each policy gives coverage to one primary driver and secondary drivers if eligible. All vehicles need to be covered under the this insurance program. A calculator is available here to see what your annual premium could be: https://www.mylowcostauto.com/get-started/coverage 
You can get this benefit if: you have a valid CA driver's license, own a vehicle valued at $25K or less, be at least 16 years old, have a good driving record, and meet income requirements (based on your husband's income, you all likely qualify for this as the max pre tax annual income limit is $107,875 for a household of 6). 
Documents you would need to provde: driver's license, current vehicle registration, initial deposit for payment, and one document for proof of income such any beneift letter from other California programs like CalFresh, CalWORKS, Lifeline, etc. or income tax returns, W-2, 1099, or payroll stub, etc.) 
To apply online: visit mylowcostauto.com and click 'Get Started' to take a short eligibility questionnaire.  If deemed eligible, enter your ZIP code, then click on Apply Online. If you do not have internet access or need additional assistance, please call 1-866-602-8861.

For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $59,547 for a household of 6). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application within 10 days. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder. 

## Covered California Details
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($59,547 to $107,875 for a household of 6), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help.If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). For the other categories, the types of documents you'd need are similar to Medi-Cal, but let me know if you want me to pull specific document types that could work. 

Keeping your benefits: 
You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 


## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

## Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) and ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you.

For help with paying for or finding child care, California has options. 

## CalWORKS Child Care Benefits 
What is it? 
- Get assistance paying for child care with a provider of your choice. 
- Child care is available for children through age 12 and for exceptional needs and severely disabled children up to age 21 

Eligibility: 
- If you currently get or previously got CalWORKs cash aid, and are currently employed or participating in a county approved Welfare-to-Work program you may be eligible 

How to apply: 
- Contact your local county welfare department to apply and learn more. If you give me your county information, I can look up your local agency for you?

## Local Child Care Resource and Referral Agency (R&R) 
What is it?
- Local Child Care Resource and Referral programs keep a list of child care providers and provides resources and information for parents looking for child care 
- Go to their website here: https://rrnetwork.org/family-services/find-child-care or call 1-800-KIDS-793 for help 

## County Alternative Payment Program (APP) 
You can reach out to community based organizations in your county to learn about alternative payment programs to help make child care affordable. Look here for more information: https://www.cappaonline.com/aps-in-california

Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($36,777 to $66,625 for a household of 3), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help.If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). For the other categories, the types of documents you'd need are similar to Medi-Cal, but let me know if you want me to pull specific document types that could work. 

Keeping your benefits: 
You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 


## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

## Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) and ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 

For help with paying for or finding child care, California has options. 

## CalWORKS Child Care Benefits 
What is it?

- Child care is available for children through age 12 and for exceptional needs and severely disabled children up to age 21 

Eligibility:

How to apply:

## Local Child Care Resource and Referral Agency (R&R) 
What is it?
- Local Child Care Resource and Referral programs keep a list of child care providers and provides resources and information for parents looking for child care 
- Go to their website here: https://rrnetwork.org/family-services/find-child-care or call 1-800-KIDS-793 for help 

## County Alternative Payment Program (APP) 
You can reach out to community based organizations in your county to learn about alternative payment programs to help make child care affordable. Look here for more information: https://www.cappaonline.com/aps-in-california

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as:

- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan

- A qualifying life event must occur

## Quick Overview
- **You can apply for California unemployment benefits** even if your husband earns $55K and you have no children.  
- Benefits are based on **your own recent earnings**, not your household income.  
- Follow the steps below to **apply, keep your claim in good standing, and avoid penalties**.

---

## 1. Determine Eligibility for Unemployment Insurance (UI)

| Requirement | What It Means for You |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Earned enough wages** | You need at least **$1,300** in one quarter of your base period **or** $900 in your highest‑earning quarter and total wages of $1,500 in the base period. |
| **Lost job through no fault of your own** | Layoff, reduction in hours, or company closure qualify. |
| **Able & available to work** | You must be ready to accept suitable work and actively look for a job. |
| **No disqualifying conduct** | No quitting without good cause, no refusal of suitable work, no fraud. |

> **Bottom line:** Your husband’s salary does **not** affect UI eligibility.

---

## 2. Apply for Unemployment Benefits

### Step‑by‑Step Guide

1. **Gather Required Documents**  
   | Document | Why It’s Needed |
   |----------|-----------------|
   | Last 4 pay stubs or W‑2s (2023‑2024) | Proves earnings |
   | Employer’s name, address, and phone | For verification |
   | Social Security Number (SSN) | Identification |
   | Driver’s license or ID card | Identity proof |
   | Bank account & routing number (for direct deposit) | Faster payment |

2. **Create an EDD Account**  
   - Go to the **California Employment Development Department (EDD)** portal: [edd.ca.gov/UI](https://edd.ca.gov/UI)  
   - Click **“Register for UI Online”** and follow the prompts.

3. **Complete the UI Claim**  
   - Fill out **UI Online** (or call 1‑800‑300‑5616 if you need assistance).  
   - Answer all questions truthfully—**misrepresenting earnings is a felony** and can lead to fines, loss of benefits, and a criminal record.

4. **Submit Weekly/Bi‑weekly Claims**  
   - After your initial claim is approved, you must **certify** each week (or every two weeks) that you are still unemployed and report any earnings.  
   - Use the **EDD UI Online** portal or the **EDD Mobile App**.

5. **Receive Your First Payment**  
   - Payments are typically **deposited within 10‑14 days** after your first certification.  
   - The amount is roughly **≈ $450‑$600 per week** (2025 rates) depending on your past wages.

---

## 3. Keep Your Claim Safe – Avoid Fines & Penalties

- **Report All Earnings** – Even a few hours of part‑time work must be reported.  
- **Certify on Time** – Missing a certification can suspend benefits and trigger a **$100‑$200 penalty**.  
- **Maintain Records** – Keep copies of pay stubs, job‑search logs, and correspondence for at least **3 years**.  
- **Respond Promptly** – If the EDD requests additional info, reply within the deadline (usually 10 days).  
- **Don’t Work “Under the Table.”** – Undocumented income is considered fraud if not reported.

---

## 4. Job‑Search Resources (Free & California‑Based)

| Resource | What It Offers | How to Access |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| **CalJOBS** | State job board, resume builder, workshops | [caljobs.ca.gov](https://www.caljobs.ca.gov) |
| **America’s Job Center (AJC)** | In‑person counseling, training, employer connections | Find your nearest center: [ajcjobs.org/centers](https://www.ajcjobs.org/centers) |
| **Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Programs** | Grants for training, apprenticeships, tuition assistance | Ask at your local AJC |
| **LinkedIn Learning (Free for UI recipients)** | Online courses to boost skills | Access via your UI portal under “Benefits & Resources” |
| **California Career Pathways** | Industry‑specific pathways (e.g., health care, tech) | [careerpathways.ca.gov](https://careerpathways.ca.gov) |

### Quick Job‑Search Checklist (Weekly)

- ☐ Apply to **5–7** new positions (online or in‑person).  
- ☐ Attend **1** networking event or virtual job fair.  
- ☐ Update your **resume** and **LinkedIn** profile.  
- ☐ Log each activity (date, employer, contact) for the EDD’s **Job‑Search Log** (required for UI).  

---

## 5. Additional Financial Assistance (If Needed)

| Program | Who Qualifies | Typical Benefit | Application Link |
|---------|---------------|----------------|------------------|
| **CalWORKs (Cash Assistance)** | Low‑income households; income limits consider household size. | Up to **$800/month** (2025). | [cdss.ca.gov/calworks](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks) |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Household income ≤ 200 % of Federal Poverty Level. | Average **$250‑$350/month** per adult. | [www.getcalfresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org) |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Adults without other income sources. | Varies by county (≈ $300‑$500/month). | Contact your county social services office. |
| **Medical Assistance (Medi‑Cal)** | Income ≤ 138 % of FPL. | Free or low‑cost health coverage. | [www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal) |

> **Tip:** You can **apply for UI and these programs simultaneously**; they do not automatically reduce UI benefits.

---

## 6. Summary of Action Items

| # | Action | Deadline |
|---|--------|----------|
| 1 | Gather pay stubs, W‑2s, ID, bank info | **Today** |
| 2 | Register on EDD UI Online & file initial claim | **Within 3 days** |
| 3 | Set up direct deposit & certify weekly | **First certification due 7 days after claim approval** |
| 4 | Create a job‑search log (Google Sheet or notebook) | **Start immediately** |
| 5 | Register on CalJOBS & schedule a visit to your nearest AJC | **Within 1 week** |
| 6 | If needed, apply for CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, or GA | **Within 2 weeks** |
| 7 | Keep all documents & logs for 3 years | Ongoing |

---

## 7. Helpful Links at a Glance

- **UI Application & Certification:** [edd.ca.gov/UI](https://edd.ca.gov/UI)  
- **CalJOBS (State Job Board):** [caljobs.ca.gov](https://www.caljobs.ca.gov)  
- **America’s Job Center Locator:** [ajcjobs.org/centers](https://www.ajcjobs.org/centers)  
- **CalFresh (SNAP) Application:** [getcalfresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)  
- **Medi‑Cal (Health Coverage):** [dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal)  

---

**You’re not alone.** California offers a robust safety net and many free resources to help you get back to work quickly and safely. Follow the steps above, stay organized, and reach out to your local America’s Job Center if you need personalized assistance. Good luck! 🌟

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

I'm sorry to hear you just got laid off. I'm here to help you find the resources you need to take care of your family.

Food Help: 
Getting food benefits does not affect you or your family's immigration status. Immigration information is private and confidential. And, good news: as a green card holder you are able to get food help. Even if you are not a US citizen, legal residents and noncitizens with certain immigration statuses can still get CalFresh. 
- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help:  https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks 
- You can apply any time for SNAP (food stamps), called CalFresh in California. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries. 
- You can apply on BenefitsCal.com or go to your county office. Online chat support is available M-F 9am to 4pm PT. 
- Your county will call within 1-2 weeks for an interview and will let you know within 30 days if you're approved. You can ask for a faster decision (expedited review) when you apply and interview. 
- If approved, you will get your EBT card for groceries within 10 days. It gets refilled monthly. 
- Documents you need: copy of your ID, proof of any income, proof of immigration status (for non-citizens) within 30 days of applying. Other optional documents could increase you benefit amount like proof of housing expenses, child or dependent care.  

Cash Aid (CalWORKs and General Assistance) 
- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. Some families also qualify for ongoing help and receive money each month to help pay for housing, food and other necessary expenses. The sooner you apply, the sooner you'll hear back on if you qualify. 
- Services vary by county but in addition to cash aid can include housing support, employment help, child care, education, mental health, substance use support, and domestic abuse support 
- You don't to be a US citizen to get cash help. Certain non-citizens may be eligible, including children born in the US even if parents are not. Applying won't affect your immigration status. California does not volunteer information about your immigration status to the federal government. 
- The amount of help you could get depends on your family's income, household size, and any special needs. Since you are taking care of children, you may qualify for more help as well like General Assistance.
- If approved for cash aid, the monthly amount gets added to your EBT card (same as CalFresh) or can be directly deposited into a bank account. 
To Apply: 
You can apply at any Social Services office in the county you live in (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/county-offices) or apply online at BenefitsCal.com. Applying through your county also checks you for other programs as well such as General Assistance.
Once you have all your documents, applying should take 30-60 minutes. Would you like me to schedule a calendar block for this time for you to apply? I can also provide a more detailed list of the documents you would need, but generally: ID, proof you live in California, money you recieve, expenses. 
Key Dates: your county will tell you the kinds of change you need to report and by when, but usually within 10 days.  To keep your benefits, your county will also reach out once a year but each program has different requirements. I can also add a reminder to your calendar a year from now? 

Unemployment Benefits can also help ease financial strain while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document)

Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. It's critical to review this information carefully and contact EDD if you see any mistakes. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

California also offers a lot of options finding a new job: 
- Workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching.

Rent or mortgage help: 
Calling 2-1-1 in California is the best way to find help to pay your rent, mortagage, utilities bills to stay in your home. Call to speak to someone right away. They will ask you a few questions about your current living situation, any income, any children or dependents who live with you. Even if you don't qualify for a government program, the state or local agency may refer you to a community organization or nonprofit in your area. 

First, you should talk with your landlord if you rent or lender if you have a mortgage to discuss your situation. There may be options like payment plans that could help you stay in your home. Housing Support: 
If you are applying for or already get CalWORKS - California's TANF program - you may also be able to get help through their Housing Support Program or Homeless Assistance program if you are experiencing homelessness now or at risk. This program is run at the county level so contact them if you would like to learn more. If you tell me your county, I can pull addresses and phone numbers for you?
The Housing Support Program can help families find temporary shelter while finding permanent housing, help with moving costs, short to medium term rent support, and a case manager to talk to and work with to get back on your feet. 
The Homeless Assistance program is more focused on helping you cover costs of keeping permanent housing providing payments every 12 months for temporary shelter, and payments to get housing including help with security deposits, last month's rent or up to 2 months of rent.

Find shelters and temporary housing through HUD programs like their local homeless assistance list, their homeless continuing care program provider, and local public housing agencies: https://www.usa.gov/emergency-housing 


There are also programs available to help with internet and phone, lower cost auto insurance, weatherizing your home, and utilities. Do you want to hear about these options as well? 

Covering phone bills: 
The California Lifeline program gives discounts on home and cell phone services to eligible households. You can get the discount on your home phone or cell phone but not on both. 
Types of Benefits: you can get up to a $19 monthly discount for flat rate service or cell phone service, a service connection discount $39, and certain taxes and user fees are made free 
Eligibility: You can qualify two ways. One way is if you or someone else in your household is already getting help from other programs like Medi-Cal, Low Income Energy Assistance Program, SSI, public hosing, CalFresh, WIC, school lunch, TANF/CalWORKs, and certain veterans program. The second way is based on income. If your household income before taxes is at or below specific limits. If your household size is 2, the max income you all can earn is $32,600 to be eligible. If you tell me more about your household size I can give more guidance. 
How to apply: First, call your home or cell phone company and tell them you qualify based on the program or income criteria above. They will begin the application for you and in a week you will get an application form in the mail in a pink envelope. Renew Benefits: You will be mailed a renewal form in another pink envelope from the California Lifeline Administrator 105 days prior to your California Lifeline anniversary date. You can renew online or fill out that application and provide any documents they ask for.

What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more

- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan

- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event.

- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it.

**What is EITC?**

The Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) is a refundable tax credit designed to help low-to-moderate-income working individuals and families. It's a benefit for people who work hard but don't earn a lot. The EITC can provide a significant refund, even if you don't owe taxes.

**Am I Eligible for EITC?**

To qualify for EITC, you must:

* Have worked and earned income from a job (like wages, salaries, or tips)
* Be a U.S. citizen or resident alien
* Have a valid Social Security number
* Meet certain income and family size requirements (see below)

**2025 EITC Income Limits and Maximum Credits**

| Family Size | Maximum Income | Maximum Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single, no children | $16,480 | $538 |
| Single, 1 child | $43,492 | $3,526 |

| Joint, 1 child | $49,399 | $3,526 |
| Joint, 2 children | $55,529 | $5,785 |
| Joint, 3 or more children | $59,399 | $6,728 |

**How to Apply for EITC**

1. **File Your Taxes**: You'll need to file your taxes to claim the EITC. You can use tax preparation software like TurboTax or H&R Block, or work with a tax professional.
2. **Use Form 1040**: When filing your taxes, use Form 1040 and complete Schedule EIC (Earned Income Credit).
3. **Gather Required Documents**: Make sure you have:
	* Your Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)
	* Your employer's name, address, and Employer Identification Number (EIN)
	* Your W-2 forms from your employer(s)
	* Your 1099 forms (if self-employed)
4. **Check Your Eligibility**: Use the IRS's [EITC Assistant](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/earned-income-tax-credit/use-the-eitc-assistant) tool to see if you qualify.
5. **Apply for Free or Low-Cost Tax Help**: If you need assistance with your taxes, consider using free or low-cost tax preparation services like:
	* [IRS Free File](https://www.irs.gov/filing/free-file-do-your-federal-taxes-for-free)
	* [Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/free-tax-return-preparation-for-qualifying-taxpayers)
	* [Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE)](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-counseling-for-the-elderly)

**Additional Resources**

* [California EITC Website](https://www.cdtfa.ca.gov/taxes-and-fees/california-earned-income-tax-credit.htm)

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

**Understanding Unemployment Insurance in California**
=====================================================

Unemployment insurance (UI) is a state-funded program that provides financial assistance to eligible workers who have lost their jobs through no fault of their own. In California, the Employment Development Department (EDD) administers the UI program.

**Eligibility Requirements**
---------------------------

To be eligible for UI benefits in California, you must:

* Have earned enough wages during the base period (the first four of the last five completed calendar quarters)
* Be unemployed through no fault of your own (e.g., laid off, downsized, or quit for good cause)
* Be actively seeking new employment
* Be ready and able to start work immediately

**How to Apply for UI Benefits**
------------------------------

1. **File a claim online**: Visit the EDD website at [edd.ca.gov](http://edd.ca.gov) and file a claim for UI benefits.
2. **Gather required documents**: You will need to provide proof of identity, employment history, and wages earned.
3. **Certify for benefits**: Once your claim is processed, you will need to certify for benefits every two weeks to continue receiving payments.

**Maximizing Your UI Benefits**
-----------------------------

1. **File your claim promptly**: The sooner you file, the sooner you can start receiving benefits.
2. **Provide accurate information**: Ensure that your application and certification forms are complete and accurate to avoid delays or denials.
3. **Actively seek new employment**: Keep a record of your job search activities, as you may be required to provide proof of your efforts.
4. **Participate in re-employment services**: Take advantage of free re-employment services, such as resume building and job placement assistance, offered by the EDD.

**UI Benefit Amounts and Duration**
---------------------------------

| **Benefit Amount** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| $40-$450 per week | The weekly benefit amount is based on your past earnings |
| 12-26 weeks | The maximum duration of UI benefits varies depending on the state's unemployment rate |

**Additional Resources**
----------------------

* **EDD Website**: [edd.ca.gov](http://edd.ca.gov)
* **UI Claimant Handbook**: A comprehensive guide to the UI program, available on the EDD website
* **Local EDD Office**: Find your nearest EDD office for in-person assistance

By understanding the UI program and following these tips, you can maximize your benefits and get back on your feet sooner.

**Debt Relief Options in California**

Losing a job can be stressful, and managing debt can be overwhelming. Fortunately, there are options available to help you get back on track. Here are some debt relief options in California:

## **Debt Counseling Agencies**

* Non-profit credit counseling agencies, such as the National Foundation for Credit Counseling (NFCC) or the Financial Counseling Association of America (FCAA), can provide you with free or low-cost advice and assistance.
* These agencies can help you create a budget, prioritize your debts, and develop a plan to pay off your debts.

## **Debt Management Plans (DMPs)**

| **DMP Benefits** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Reduced interest rates | Creditors may lower interest rates to help you pay off debt faster |
| Waived fees | Creditors may waive late fees or other charges |
| Consolidated payments | Make one monthly payment to the credit counseling agency |
| Credit score improvement | Completing a DMP can help improve your credit score |

## **Debt Consolidation Loans**

* If you have good credit, you may be able to consolidate your debts into a single loan with a lower interest rate and a longer repayment period.
* Be cautious of debt consolidation loans with high interest rates or fees.

## **California Debt Collection Laws**

* California has laws that protect consumers from debt collectors, such as the Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act.
* Debt collectors must follow specific guidelines when contacting you, and you have the right to dispute debts and request validation.

## **Bankruptcy**

* If you're overwhelmed with debt and can't see a way out, bankruptcy may be an option.
* Chapter 7 bankruptcy can discharge some debts, while Chapter 13 bankruptcy can help you create a repayment plan.

## **Additional Resources**

* [California Department of Business Oversight](https://dbo.ca.gov/): Provides information on debt collection laws and regulations in California.
* [National Foundation for Credit Counseling](https://www.nfcc.org/): Offers non-profit credit counseling and education.

**Job Search Assistance in California**

After a layoff, it's essential to know where to turn for help finding a new job. California offers various resources to support you in your job search. Here are some options:

### **America's Job Center of California (AJCC)**

*   A network of centers providing free employment services, including job search assistance, resume building, and interview preparation.
*   AJCCs also offer information on training programs, education, and career development.
*   You can find your local AJCC by visiting the [California Employment Development Department (EDD) website](https://www.edd.ca.gov/Office_Locator/AJCC.htm).

### **California Employment Development Department (EDD)**

*   The EDD website offers a range of job search tools, including CalJOBS, a job search platform that allows you to search for jobs, upload your resume, and receive job match notifications.
*   You can also file for unemployment benefits and access information on job training programs through the EDD website.

### **Local Workforce Development Boards**

*   These boards provide job search assistance, training programs, and education to help you find employment.
*   You can find your local Workforce Development Board by visiting the [California Workforce Development Board website](https://www.cwdb.ca.gov/).

### **Non-Profit Organizations**

*   Organizations like the **United Way** and **Goodwill** offer job search assistance, resume building, and interview preparation.
*   These organizations may also provide access to job training programs and education.

**Connecting to Benefits**

Many of these resources can connect you to benefits, including:

| Benefit | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Unemployment Insurance | Financial assistance for eligible workers who have lost their job through no fault of their own. |
| CalFresh | A food assistance program for low-income individuals and families. |
| Medi-Cal | A health insurance program for low-income individuals and families. |
| Job Training Programs | Programs that provide training and education to help you find employment. |

When visiting these resources, be sure to ask about the benefits you may be eligible for.

Unemployment Benefits can help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)

--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively).

Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

["## More help with medical bills after insurance

Charity care - If you still need help with medical bills after health insurance or Medicaid payments have been applied, a charity care program may assist you with the remaining costs. In most cases, you can apply for charity care through a doctor or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Learn more about charity care and how it works.", 
"## Get help paying for prescription drugs

- Contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your prescription drugs or devices. Ask them about low-cost options, samples, or discounts.

["## Steps to take for charity care or financial help with medical bills

Ask for a copy of the hospital’s financial assistance policy up front. By law, the policy must be provided free of charge and must tell you how to apply for help. You can ask whether the policy is available in your preferred language in addition to English.
- Fill out the application with information about your income, including last year’s tax forms or a current pay stub, and your expenses, including your rent or mortgage payment, utilities, credit cards, and other expenses.
- Ask your provider how long it takes to process your application for financial assistance, how to get answers to questions about the application, and what happens with your bill in the meantime.

**Understanding Your Benefits in California**

Losing a job can be challenging, but California offers various benefits to support you during this transition. We'll break down how severance, part-time gig work, unemployment benefits, and Medi-Cal interact.

### Severance and Unemployment Benefits

In California, receiving a severance package does not necessarily disqualify you from receiving unemployment benefits. However, the timing and amount of your severance can impact your eligibility.

* If your severance is paid in a lump sum, it may not affect your unemployment benefits.
* If your severance is paid over time, it may be considered income and could reduce or delay your unemployment benefits.

To determine how your severance affects your unemployment benefits, you'll need to:

1. File a claim for unemployment benefits with the [California Employment Development Department (EDD)](https://edd.ca.gov/).
2. Report your severance payment when you file your claim or during your bi-weekly certification.

### Part-time Gig Work and Unemployment Benefits

Part-time gig work can also impact your unemployment benefits. In California, you can work part-time and still receive unemployment benefits, but your earnings may reduce the amount of your benefits.

* You must report all your earnings, including gig work, when you certify for benefits.
* The EDD will calculate your benefits based on your reported earnings.

### Medi-Cal Eligibility

Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program, which provides health coverage to low-income individuals and families. If you're receiving unemployment benefits, you may be eligible for Medi-Cal.

* Your eligibility for Medi-Cal is based on your income and family size.
* You can apply for Medi-Cal through the [California Department of Health Care Services](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/) or through [Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/).

| Unemployment Benefits | File a claim with the EDD, meet eligibility requirements |
| Medi-Cal | Apply through DHCS or Covered California, meet income and family size requirements |

### Next Steps

1. File a claim for unemployment benefits with the EDD.
2. Report your severance payment and part-time gig work earnings when you certify for benefits.
3. Apply for Medi-Cal through DHCS or Covered California.

By following these steps, you can navigate the process and understand how your severance, part-time gig work, and unemployment benefits interact with your eligibility for Medi-Cal.

**Reapplying for WIC after Job Loss: Timelines, Documents, and Unemployment Benefits**

If you have an appeal pending on a denial and reapply for WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) after a job loss, here are the key timelines, documents, and information regarding your unemployment benefits:

### Timelines

* **WIC Application Processing Time**: Typically, WIC applications are processed within 2-4 weeks. However, this timeframe may vary depending on the local WIC agency's workload and the completeness of your application.
* **Appeal Pending**: If you have an appeal pending on a previous denial, it's essential to inform the WIC agency about the status of your appeal. This may affect the processing time of your new application.

### Documents

* **Proof of Income**: You will need to provide proof of your current income, which may include:
	+ Unemployment benefits award letter
	+ Pay stubs (if you're receiving partial unemployment benefits)
	+ Letter from your former employer stating your last date of work and income
* **Proof of Identity**: You will need to provide a valid government-issued ID, such as a driver's license or passport.
* **Proof of Residency**: You will need to provide proof of California residency, such as a utility bill or lease agreement.
* **Proof of Pregnancy or Child's Age**: If you're applying for WIC benefits for a child, you will need to provide proof of the child's age, such as a birth certificate.

### Unemployment Benefits

* **Reapplying for WIC will not affect your unemployment benefits**: The WIC program and unemployment benefits are separate programs. Reapplying for WIC will not impact your eligibility for unemployment benefits.
* **Reporting Changes**: If you're receiving unemployment benefits, you must report any changes in your income or employment status to the California Employment Development Department (EDD). However, reapplying for WIC is not considered a change in employment status.

### Additional Resources

* **California WIC Program**: For more information on the WIC program, eligibility, and application process, visit the [California WIC Program website](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CWLP/Pages/default.aspx).
* **California Employment Development Department (EDD)**: For information on unemployment benefits, visit the [EDD website](https://www.edd.ca.gov/).

Remember to contact your local WIC agency for specific guidance on the application process and required documents.

For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $59,547 for a household of 6). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up.

- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder. 

## Covered California Details
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($59,547 to $107,875 for a household of 6), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help.If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer.

Keeping your benefits: 
You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 


## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it.

If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator.
